title: Pre-paint scroll lock becomes PERMANENT if the JS bundle fails to hydrate — visitor is trapped on a black, unscrollable page
evidence: app/layout.tsx:122 adds `gcl-prologue` from an inline pre-paint script; app/globals.css:446 makes it `overflow:hidden`; the ONLY code that removes it is `awaken()` inside the React component (components/ArrivalScene.tsx:248). The inline script always runs; the component may never mount. Measured with Playwright route-abort on the main bundle: R4 with `**/_next/static/chunks/main-app-*.js` blocked -> html="js gcl-prologue", overflow=hidden, document 9619px tall, and a real mouse wheel(0,1500) followed by End leaves scrollY=0. Identical result with `**/_next/static/chunks/app/page-*.js` blocked. CONTROL under the exact same block: overflow=visible, scrollY=8719 — the whole site remains readable. Screenshot /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-re3zy/b1a3eebd-71bd-4681-8fbe-fedeec4d6c0a/scratchpad/rgate/shots/trap-r4-nojs.png shows the result: a black screen with only a 1.1%-opacity ghost of the mark (the new LCP floor), no nav, no skip chip (the CSS gate holds it at visibility:hidden and GSAP never runs to reveal it), and no way to scroll. Note this is strictly worse than the true no-JS case, which the design handles correctly because `html.js` is never added.
fix: The element that applies the lock must be able to release it without React. Simplest: have the same inline script arm its own watchdog, e.g. append `setTimeout(function(){document.documentElement.classList.remove('gcl-prologue')},18000);` so the lock is self-expiring in every failure mode. Alternatively move the lock into the mount effect that owns `awaken()` (costing one scrollable frame), or require a second class that only the hydrated component sets (`html.gcl-prologue.gcl-armed { overflow:hidden }`). Add a regression test that blocks a chunk and asserts the page still scrolls.

title: Crossing 1024px mid-prologue strands a mobile-width visitor: scroll-locked for up to ~13s in a desktop composition, with no escape before ~3s
evidence: `isDesktopWidthNow` and `willRunPrologue` are computed once at mount (components/ArrivalScene.tsx:160,174) and never re-evaluated; the prologue timeline is built in the `isDesktopWidthNow` branch (line 273) outside any gsap.matchMedia, so nothing aborts it. Measured 1440x900 -> 390x844 at t=3.0s (mid P2): `html.gcl-prologue` and overflow:hidden persist until wall ~13s; the DESKTOP timeline keeps playing on the 390px viewport — gold signal hairline drawn to 0.55, atmosphere at 0.08 then breathing, mark withheld until +5s, tagline until +13s, nav until +13s. Crossing at t=1.5s is worse: the skip chip reads opacity 0 / visibility hidden / pointer-events none with elementsFromPoint confirming skipClickable=false, and a touch device has no Esc key — zero escape affordance. Real user input is genuinely blocked in every case: wheel(0,800) and End+PageDown both leave scrollY=0 (control scrolls to 800 and 8501). Reproduced under desktop-reduce too (pins correctly drop to 0, but the page is still locked ~10s while an animating gold hairline and a breathing atmosphere play — channels mobile-reduce must never see). CONTROL never locks at any crossing and composes by ~2.5s. Real-world triggers: tablet rotation across the 1024px line, window resize, and browser zoom (Chrome fires resize on zoom, so a low-vision visitor zooming in during the prologue is stranded). Secondary: the crossing permanently leaks prologue-only inline styles into the mobile composition that a native 390px load never has — `.arrival__atmosphere{opacity:0.08}`, `.arrival__signal{transform;opacity}`, `.arrival__skip{pointer-events:auto;opacity:1;visibility:inherit}` — breaking the R3 mobile gate's 'zero inline-style leaks across breakpoint crossings'.
fix: Make the prologue abort on its own breakpoint. Either build it inside a `gsap.matchMedia` keyed on `(min-width:1024px)` so GSAP tears it down on the crossing, or add a `matchMedia('(min-width:1024px)').addEventListener('change', ...)` handler that, on leaving desktop, calls `tl.progress(1,false)` (which already runs awaken() and unlocks) and clears the atmosphere/signal inline styles. Also remove the Esc keydown listener on the same transition. Then re-run the R3 mobile hard gate (pins 0/2, pixel parity, zero inline leaks) with a mid-prologue crossing included.

title: Keyboard Tab escapes the locked prologue: scrolls 6,754px into the page and force-reveals the nav 9s early
evidence: Full-motion 1440x900, R4 build. At t=3.6s (skip chip visible) I pressed Tab 8 times and sampled document.activeElement plus scroll state after each. Tab 1 = A.skip-link, Tab 2 = BUTTON.arrival__skip (correct), Tab 3 = A.ecosystem__wing-link with scrollY jumping 0 -> 6754, Tab 4 -> scrollY 12772 (footer). html{overflow:hidden} does not block focus-driven scrolling. Re-sampled immediately after the 3rd Tab: {lock:true, htmlOverflow:"hidden", scrollY:6754, nav:"0.6124", markWrap:"0.0110", signal:"0.4293", glow:"0.3828", cue:"0.0000"} — i.e. the scroll lock is nominally on, the prologue is still mid-P2/P3, and Nav.tsx's scrollY>60 rule has already begun revealing the nav at 3.6s instead of awaken()'s 12.8s, breaking P1's "no UI" for the rest of the run. The live region still reads "Introduction playing — press Escape to skip at any time." while the visitor is looking at the Ecosystem section. After the timeline completed I re-sampled: scrollY still 6754, awake:true, cue:"0.0000" — the composition resolves against an arbitrary scroll position. The control build scrolls on Tab too (scrollY 6214) but has no lock and no no-UI phase, so this is an R4-introduced contradiction, not inherited behaviour. Neither implementer report nor the verification pass mentions tabbing during the prologue.
fix: While html.gcl-prologue is applied, make the rest of the document non-focusable rather than only non-scrollable: set the `inert` attribute on the main content wrapper and footer when the pre-paint script adds the class, and remove it inside awaken() alongside classList.remove('gcl-prologue'). That fixes the focus escape, the premature nav reveal (no scroll => no scrollY>60 trip) and the AT reading-order problem in one move, and keeps the skip chip + skip-link reachable because both live outside the inert subtree. Verify by re-running the Tab sweep: focus must cycle within {skip-link, arrival__skip} and scrollY must stay 0 until awaken().

title: Desktop-to-mobile viewport crossing mid-prologue strands the visitor scroll-locked on a wrong-breakpoint black screen for ~9s
evidence: Loaded R4 at 1440x900 full-motion, then setViewportSize(390x844) at t=3.2s (mid-P2). Sampled every 2s while issuing a mouse wheel of 600px and reading scrollY. Results: t=3.68s lock=true overflow=hidden mark=0.0000 glow=0.0000 scrollYafterWheel=0; identical at t=5.08s, 7.08s (mark 0.9662 by then), 9.08s, 11.08s — scroll blocked at every sample. Lock only released at t=13.08s when the DESKTOP timeline's own awaken() fired, i.e. ~9.4s stranded. Screenshot at t=5s (saved to scratchpad/r4gate/resize-mobile-5s.png) shows a 390px-wide near-black frame with only the gold hairline and the SKIP chip. The mark reads exactly 0 rather than the desktop 0.011 floor because the LCP floor is scoped to @media(min-width:1024px), so the crossing removes it. Root cause in components/ArrivalScene.tsx: `const isDesktopWidthNow = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)").matches;` and `willRunPrologue` are computed once inside the mount effect with a [] dependency array and never re-evaluated. iPad Pro 11" (1194 landscape / 834 portrait) and iPad Air (1180 / 820) both cross 1024px on rotation, so a rotation during the 14.4s prologue reproduces this. Violates the mission's 'mobile keeps its current arrival COMPLETELY UNCHANGED'.
fix: Add a matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)') change listener that, when the query stops matching while the prologue is still running, aborts cleanly: timelineRef.current?.progress(1, false) (which fires the intervening revealSkip/awaken calls, releasing the lock and composing the scene) — the same escape path Esc already uses. Guard it with completedRef so it cannot double-fire. Re-run the resize probe and assert lock=false and a non-zero scrollY within one frame of the crossing.

title: Replay does not deliver the full prologue: chrome visible from frame 1, atmosphere never resets, and the SKIP chip's clicks are hijacked by a nav link
evidence: Three separate measured defects on the replay path (full-motion 1440x900, after one complete first play). (a) ATMOSPHERE NEVER RESETS: setInitialHiddenStates writes gsap.set(atmosphere,{opacity:0}) inline, but `awake` is set once and never unset, so `.arrival--awake .arrival__atmosphere{animation:gcl-atmosphere-breathe}` stays active — CSS animations outrank inline style declarations in the cascade. Measured through a replay: t=155ms atm=0.0692, t=1406 atm=0.0780, t=2407 atm=0.0855, t=5004 atm=0.0987. P1's tl.to(atmosphere,{opacity:0.08}) is therefore a silent no-op on every replay, and the 'void breathes to barely-visible' beat is absent. (b) CHROME PRESENT: screenshot at replay t=2400ms (scratchpad/r4gate/replay-P1-2400.png) shows the full nav bar with brand mark and all six links, the gold REPLAY ARRIVAL chip, and a SKIP chip at opacity 1.000 from t=155ms (revealSkip's inline autoAlpha from the first play is never reset). P1's 'Darkness. Silence. No UI, no nav, no text' is entirely absent from every replay. (c) SKIP CLICK HIJACKED: .arrival__skip is z-index 20 (globals.css:678) and header.nav is z-index 600 (globals.css:244). During replay the header is opacity 1 / pointer-events auto, so document.elementsFromPoint at the chip's centre returns [A.nav__link, NAV.nav__links, HEADER.nav, BUTTON.arrival__skip] — the chip is 4th. A real page.mouse.click at the chip centre navigated to http://127.0.0.1:4190/#contact and jumped to scrollY 11267 while the replay was still at P1 (markWrap 0.0110, tagline 0). The header also carries backdrop-filter: blur(10px), so the chip is visually smeared as well. The z-order half reproduces on the control build (control replay also returns A.nav__link on top), so that specific defect is inherited from R3 — but R4 is what makes the skip affordance load-bearing.
fix: (a) Clear the awake class for the duration of a replay — setAwake(false) in handleReplay before tl.play(0), letting awaken() set it true again at P6; that restores GSAP's authority over the atmosphere. (b) Reset the skip chip in handleReplay with gsap.set(skipButtonRef.current,{autoAlpha:0,pointerEvents:'none'}) so P2's revealSkip is a real reveal again, and decide explicitly whether a replay should re-add gcl-prologue (the current code comments say no; the mission's 'Replay Arrival = full prologue' says yes — Founder call). (c) Raise .arrival__skip above the nav (z-index 700, or any value above 600) so the mandated affordance is never occluded or click-hijacked in any state.

title: The new refresh-reclaim listener stomps the accepted R3 pull-back scene on every later ScrollTrigger.refresh() — glow snaps to full and the ENTER cue reappears
evidence: components/ArrivalScene.tsx:616-627 registers `reclaimPrologueGlow` on ScrollTrigger's global "refresh" event for the entire page lifetime at >=1024px. Once `tl.time() >= GLOW_REVEAL_AT` (4.8), its else-branch runs `tl.render(tl.time(), true, true)` — a FORCE re-render of the whole prologue timeline at its end frame, which re-stamps glow=1 and cue=1 over whatever the pull-back's scrub currently owns. Measured with a real setViewportSize resize (the same event a window drag, devtools dock, or browser-zoom change produces), visitor parked at y=450 inside the Arrival pull-back: R4 first-visit post-prologue -> glow 0.625 -> 1 and cue 0 -> 1 within 250ms; R4 seen-path desktop-reduce at y=300 -> glow 0.5833 -> 1 and cue 0 -> 1. CONTROL is unchanged in all three configurations (glow held at 0.625 / 0.5833, cue held at 0) through both a resize and an explicit ScrollTrigger.refresh(). Wrong values persist until the next scroll event. Visual proof: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-re3zy/b1a3eebd-71bd-4681-8fbe-fedeec4d6c0a/scratchpad/rgate/shots/r4-B-after-resize.png shows the 'ENTER' cue re-drawn at full opacity mid-pull-back and the mark's glow at full brightness; ctl-B-after-resize.png at the identical scroll position shows neither. This regresses the same element R3 Finding 3 was raised about.
fix: Scope the listener to the window where it is actually needed. Add an early return once the prologue is done — `if (completedRef.current) return;` — and/or remove the listener inside `awaken()`/`markComplete` via `ScrollTrigger.removeEventListener("refresh", reclaimPrologueGlow)`. Never `render(..., force=true)` a timeline whose targets another live ScrollTrigger owns. Re-run the resize-at-y=450 comparison against control as the regression test.

title: The scroll lock is one-directional: a Tab press escapes it and the keyboard visitor cannot get back
evidence: `overflow:hidden` blocks wheel and keys but not the browser's own focus scroll-into-view. Measured on R4 at t=1.2s (P1): three Tab presses move focus to off-screen links and scroll the page to y=12772 on a 13672px document while overflow is still `hidden`; a subsequent real wheel(0,-4000) plus Home leaves scrollY at 12772 — the visitor is stranded at the footer for the rest of the prologue. CONTROL under identical input: 3 Tabs -> y=6214, then wheel-up + Home returns cleanly to y=0. Two further consequences measured in the same run: nav opacity rises to 1 during P1 (Nav.tsx reveals on scrollY>60), breaking the Founder's 'P1 = no UI' requirement; and the entire cinematic prologue then plays off-screen while the visitor looks at the footer. For contrast, with no interaction the P1 no-UI rule holds perfectly (nav opacity 0 at 0.4/1.2/2.4/5.0/9.0/12.5s, 0.994 at 13.4s).
fix: Either make the lock symmetric — add a `scroll` handler while `gcl-prologue` is set that re-asserts `window.scrollTo(0,0)`, or `position:fixed; inset:0` the scrolling container instead of `overflow:hidden` — or accept focus-scroll and make the prologue skip itself the moment focus leaves the arrival section (a `focusin` handler outside `section.arrival` calling `tl.progress(1,false)`), which is the friendlier reading of the a11y mitigation the Founder asked for.

title: Mobile arrival composition changed beyond the disclosure, the disclosed magnitude is wrong, and the tagline wraps with an orphan at 320px
evidence:
Measured R4 vs git-archive control at 320/390/768, both motion policies, after full composition. Structural gate passes: pin counts identical (2/2 no-preference, 0/0 reduce), document heights byte-identical (320: 10165/10165 and 7592/7592; 390: 9631/9631 and 7059/7059; 768: 9785/9785 and 7617/7617), inline-style counts differ by exactly 1 (the removed

), atmosphere and signal both computed 0 at every mobile combination. But the composition moved: vertical delta on markTop/wordTop/tagTop/stageTop is 2.80px @320, 14.21px @390, 16.03px @768 — NOT the uniform '14px at 390/320/768, both motion policies' Implementer A disclosed, and off by 5x at 320. There is also an entirely undisclosed HORIZONTAL component: .arrival__stage width grows by 11.7px @320, 67.37px @390, 57.55px @768, because the Founder's single line is longer than either line it replaced and the stage is a shrink-to-fit flex item. Consequences: at 320px the 'single line' does not fit and wraps to two visual lines (tagline block height 46px = 2 x 23px) breaking as '...for Intelligent / Capital.' — an orphan, where the control rendered two balanced 268px lines (screenshots scratchpad/r4gate/mobile/320-R4.png vs 320-CTRL.png). At 390px the line measures 336px inside a 390px viewport (86% edge-to-edge) against the control's 268px (69%). glowTop and cueTop deltas are 0, so the ripple is confined to the stage stack, but this is a HARD CONSTRAINT ('mobile keeps its current arrival COMPLETELY UNCHANGED') and the Founder would be signing off on numbers that do not match the pixels at two of three breakpoints.
fix: Founder decision on scope first: the COPY RULING was specified for the prologue's P5, and applying it to mobile is Implementer A's own interpretation. Either (a) scope arrival.tagline to the desktop prologue and leave the mobile arrival on the existing pair, restoring true mobile parity, or (b) keep it sitewide and repair the typography — set a max-width / text-wrap: balance on .arrival__tagline-line at mobile widths so 320px breaks cleanly instead of orphaning 'Capital.', and pull 390px back off the gutters. Either way, re-measure and re-disclose the per-breakpoint deltas (2.80 / 14.21 / 16.03px vertical, 11.7 / 67.4 / 57.6px horizontal) rather than the single 14px figure.

title: The 0.011 LCP floor ghosts the mark AND the wordmark through P1-P4, and the wordmark half of it is provably unnecessary
evidence: Isolated by A/B pixel diff: rendered the same instants with the floor forced to 0 and diffed raw pixels. The wordmark floor alone contributes 3,628 changed pixels at max channel delta 3, bbox [531,511,909,558] (the GABRIEL glyph band), at t=1200ms, t=2400ms and t=9000ms — i.e. through P1 ('No UI, no nav, no text') and through P4 ('The G exists alone'). The mark floor contributes the remainder (~11,800px, max delta 3-4, bbox from y=231). Absolute values: background is RGB(6,6,8); mark and wordmark regions peak at RGB(10,10,12) during P1. Faint, but a large-area 4/255 step near black is at the edge of visibility on an OLED in a dark room, and it means P3 reveals a G that was already faintly present rather than one emerging from nothing. Crucially the wordmark floor buys nothing: I measured LCP with PerformanceObserver(buffered:true), 2 runs each, with the wordmark forced to 0 — AS-SHIPPED 284/352ms, MARK-ONLY at 0.011 352/268ms, MARK-ONLY at 0.002 364/264ms, all reporting the same element IMG.arrival__mark size 56632; BOTH-ZERO produced no LCP entry at all, confirming the mechanism is real but that a single non-zero candidate is sufficient. Broader LCP headline independently confirmed across 3 runs each: R4 desktop 248-356ms (both policies) vs control 1248-1256ms; mobile unchanged (R4 1252-1260 vs control 1240-1252).
fix: Drop the wordmark rule from the @media (min-width: 1024px) block in globals.css — keep `html.js .arrival__mark-wrap{opacity:0.011}`, delete `html.js .arrival__wordmark-top{opacity:0.011}`. That removes the only text on screen during P1 and restores 'the G exists alone' in P4 at zero LCP cost (measured above). Optionally lower the mark floor toward 0.002, which also still registers as an LCP candidate and roughly quarters the remaining ghost.

title: The SKIP chip is the brightest element on screen during the prologue's most restrained phases
evidence: Raw pixel measurement of the captured frames. At t=4.8s (peak of P2, the 'restrained gold signal, almost invisible, not decorative' phase) the SKIP chip's brightest pixel is RGB(183,183,183) while the gold signal's brightest is RGB(119,91,42) — the chip is ~55% brighter than the phase's hero element, and it is a cool neutral grey inside a scene whose entire palette is obsidian and gold. At t=3.2s, immediately after it appears, the chip already reads RGB(129,129,129) against a signal at RGB(14,11,10). Confirmed visually in scratchpad/r4gate/frames-no-preference/04802.png, where the chip is the first thing the eye goes to. The styling is inherited (globals.css:674 border rgba(183,183,183,0.35), color stone-silver) and was fine when it sat over a composed page, but the prologue puts it over near-total darkness. Contrast headroom: RGB(183,183,183) on RGB(6,6,8) is roughly 9:1, versus the 4.5:1 AA threshold reached at about RGB(118,118,118) — so it can be dimmed substantially without any accessibility cost.
fix: Reveal the chip to a lower target inside revealSkip() (e.g. autoAlpha 0.55-0.65 rather than 1), or give it a prologue-scoped treatment under html.gcl-prologue using the gold token at reduced alpha, restoring full weight on :hover/:focus-visible. Keep the computed contrast above 4.5:1 against #060608 and re-measure. This preserves the Founder's mandated affordance while letting P2's gold signal actually be the brightest thing in P2.

title: The LCP floor introduces the site's only axe violation: serious color-contrast on the wordmark for ~10.6s, in both motion policies
evidence: app/globals.css:600-603 sets `html.js .arrival__mark-wrap` and `html.js .arrival__wordmark-top` to `opacity: 0.011` at >=1024px. That turns 'GABRIEL' into a rendered-but-unreadable text node rather than a hidden one. axe-core 4.10 (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, best-practice) at t=2.0s: R4 full-motion = 1 serious `color-contrast` on `.arrival__wordmark-top`; R4 desktop-reduce = the same 1 violation. CONTROL = 0 violations at every sampled time in every policy (its opacity:0 makes the node non-visible to axe). R4 is clean again at t=16s and clean on mobile. The condition lasts from first paint until the P5 word reveal completes at ~10.6s on every first desktop visit.
fix: Keep the floor on the IMAGE (which carries LCP anyway and has no contrast rule) and return `.arrival__wordmark-top` to `opacity: 0` — measure whether LCP still lands on IMG.arrival__mark, which it did in every one of my runs. If the text floor is genuinely load-bearing, add `aria-hidden` plus a `color-contrast` axe exclusion for the prologue window and record it as an accepted, time-boxed exception rather than an unreported one.

title: The disclosed mobile shift is materially wrong: not 14px uniform, and it has an undisclosed horizontal component
evidence: Implementer A's report states 'measured 14px at 390/320/768px, both motion policies' and asks the Founder to accept that number. Direct measurement of the rendered positions (R4 vs control, both fully composed, viewport height held constant): 320px = 2.80px, 390px = 14.21px, 768px = 16.03px — non-uniform and 5x wrong at 320. Undisclosed entirely: `.arrival__stage` and `.arrival__tagline-line` change BOX WIDTH between builds by +11.7px @320, +67.37px @390, +78.28px @768, with a matching x-offset shift (the stage is a non-stretched flex item whose shrink-to-fit width depends on the tagline's line count). Full-page PNG diff of the arrival viewport (own decoder, per-pixel, threshold 2): 4.99% @320, 4.87% @390, 3.67% @768 of pixels differ, all confined to rows containing the mark/wordmark/tagline block. Everything else on mobile is genuinely clean and I confirm it: document height byte-identical at all 6 width/policy combos, pin counts identical (2/2 no-preference, 0/0 reduce), glow/cue/pin boxes unchanged (dx=dy=dw=0), and the scrolled-page diff is exactly 0 at 320 and 390 no-preference.
fix: Correct the disclosure with the three real numbers plus the horizontal component before asking for sign-off. If the Founder wants parity restored, give `.arrival__tagline` a `min-height` equal to two lines at mobile widths and set an explicit `width:100%` on `.arrival__stage` so its box stops depending on tagline line count — then re-run the PNG diff and expect the delta to collapse to the tagline glyphs alone.

title: The prologue's aria-live status never resolves — screen-reader users are told the introduction is still playing after it has ended
evidence: components/ArrivalScene.tsx:400 sets the live region to 'Introduction playing — press Escape to skip at any time.' on a first-visit prologue, and nothing ever clears it: `markComplete` (lines 212-216) only speaks when `wasReplayRef.current` is true, which is set exclusively by an explicit Replay. Measured: after Esc at 1.2s, 3.6s and 9.0s (full-motion) and 3.6s (desktop-reduce), the region still reads 'Introduction playing — press Escape to skip at any time.'; same after a chip click and after a chip Enter; CONTROL's region is empty in the equivalent state. Related and also measured (pre-existing in control, so not a regression but relevant to the same journey): activating the skip chip with Enter drops focus to <body> in both builds, because markComplete sets `hidden` on the focused button — the same defect class R3 Finding 16 fixed for the Replay chip.
fix: In `markComplete`, when the prologue actually ran, replace the text — e.g. `setAnnouncement("Introduction complete — the page is ready")` — gated so it does not fire on the seen/hash progress(1) jump. While there, move focus off the skip chip before hiding it (`headingRef.current?.focus({preventScroll:true})`), reusing the Finding-16 pattern.

title: P4's held frame is 2.2s of genuine stillness — at the short end for 'the symbol is remembered'
evidence: Sampled every 200ms across the full sequence. The last moving value settles at t=7.80s (glow and markWrap both reach exactly 1.0000; the signal reached 0 at 7.40s) and the first word beat starts at t=10.00s (wordTop 0 -> 0.1444 at 10.21s). Every layer is byte-stable across the 7.80-10.00s window: atmosphere 0.0800, signal 0, glow 1, markWrap 1, wordTop 0.0110, wordBottom 0, tagline 0, nav 0, cue 0. That is 2.2s of true hold inside a 14.4s total. Nothing is wrong mechanically — the empty dwell tween works exactly as specified — but the Founder's direction was 'Do not rush', and 2.2s sits at the low end of the 2-4s a studio ident typically holds a resolved mark.
fix: If you want more weight, push the P5 word positions later (wordTop 9.6 -> 10.6, wordBottom 10.4 -> 11.4, tagline 11.3 -> 12.3) and move the P6 awaken call from 12.4 to 13.4, extending the empty dwell at 8.0 from 1.6 to 2.6. Total becomes 15.4s wall — still inside the Founder's 12-16s window — and the hold becomes 3.2s. Purely a taste call; no other beat needs to move.

title: The institution now presents two different official taglines depending on surface
evidence: Verified by fetching both builds: the R4 arrival renders 'Building the Infrastructure for Intelligent Capital.' as its only visible tagline (taglineCount 1 at every width), while <title> remains 'Gabriel Capital Labs — Building Intelligent Infrastructure.' — byte-identical to the control — and layout.tsx:68 still emits organizationJsonLd slogan = site.tagline.join(' ') = 'Building Intelligent Infrastructure. Engineering the Future of Intelligence.' A hash-normalized diff of the two builds' <head> blocks shows the ONLY differences are Next.js chunk filenames, so the SEO non-negotiable was honoured exactly as instructed. grep confirms site.tagline now has exactly one consumer (the JSON-LD slogan) and appears nowhere in visible body copy, so there is no on-page double tagline. The consequence is external: a browser tab, a search result and a social share card state one tagline while the site's own opening statement states another.
fix: No code change required — this is the disclosed, instructed trade-off. Founder confirm only: either accept the split (arrival speaks the new line, SEO surfaces keep the old), or schedule a separate SEO-owned change to align title/description/slogan, which must go through its own ranking-risk review rather than riding along with R4.

title: The pre-paint lock ships on every route, including 404.html, which has no ArrivalScene to unlock it
evidence: The inline script lives in app/layout.tsx and therefore emits into every generated page. Measured at /404.html on a desktop-width first visit: html="js gcl-prologue", overflow=hidden, hasArrival=false — nothing on that page can ever remove the class. It is harmless today only because the 404 page happens to be exactly one viewport tall (docH 900 = vh 900), so there is nothing to scroll. CONTROL's /404.html is overflow:visible. Any future route, or a 404 page that grows past one viewport, inherits a permanent lock.
fix: Gate the predicate on being the arrival page — e.g. `location.pathname === '/'` — in the inline script, in addition to the width/hash/session checks it already mirrors from `willRunPrologue`. The watchdog from finding 1 also covers this.
